# ACUTE BACTERIAL PROSTATITIS

Acute bacterial prostatitis (ABP) typically presents with fever, dysuria, chills, malaise, myalgia, pelvic or perianal pain. On exam, the prostate gland is tense, boggy, and extremely tender. The urinalysis reveals pyuria, and the urine culture is positive. Men with dysuria and fever but without pyuria and/or bacteriuria should be seen by a urologist. If there is any suspicion of abscess, the patient should be seen by a urologist.
Those with recent urinary tract instrumentation or surgery (e.g., prostate biopsy, vasectomy) are associated with enteric Gram-negative rods. There are cases of ABP associated with N. gonorrhoeae and C. trachomatis. Resistant organisms are more likely if the patient has been in the hospital for more than 48 hours or received a course of antibiotics. There is increasing resistance in urinary pathogens to fluroquinolones.
A midstream urine sample before antibiotics are taken and send for culture and susceptibility testing should be performed in all patients to guide antimicrobial therapy. When S. aureus is recovered from a urine culture, it is important to perform blood cultures to evaluate whether the bacteriuria reflects seeding of the prostate or urine from bacteremia.

## Duration

Patients at risk of sexually transmitted infections should be assessed for treatment.
[Sexually Transmitted Infections and HIV Exposure](sexually-transmitted-infection)
Duration of therapy for ABP is usually 2 weeks, although it can be continued for up to 4 weeks for severe illness or treatment of patients with concomitant bacteremia.

Therapy:
## Inpatient

### Empirical treatment

Give oral antibiotics first line if the person can take oral medicines, and the severity of their condition does not require intravenous antibiotics.
1st choice:
Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO q12h ($) [R,DI]
< OR >
Levofloxacin 750 mg IV q24h ($) [R, DI] for 14 days

*Local guidance (Omaha CDSS, Inpatient):*
Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV q12h ($) [R,DI]
< OR >
Levofloxacin 750 mg PO q24h ($) [R,DI]
< OR >
Levofloxacin 750 mg IV q24h ($) [R, DI]
Alternate 1st choice:
Trimethoprim/sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet q12h ($) [R,DI]

## Outpatient

### Empirical treatment

Give oral antibiotics first line if the person can take oral medicines, and the severity of their condition does not require intravenous antibiotics.
1st choice:
Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO q12h ($) [R,DI] for 14 days

Patients weighing 300 lbs or greater:
Ceftriaxone 1 gm IM once ($) [M] <AND> doxycycline 100 mg PO q12h ($) [DI] for 14 days

### Age >/= 35 years

Preferred:
Levofloxacin 750 mg PO q24h ($) [R, DI] for 14 days
< OR >
Levofloxacin 750 mg IV q24h ($) [R, DI] for 14 days
